title: CareVista Hospitals to inaugurate 450-bed multi-specialty hospital in Hyderabad's Kokapet
body: CareVista Hospitals will inaugurate a 450-bed multi-specialty hospital in Kokapet, Hyderabad, in the first week of January, the group said on Monday. The INR 950 crore greenfield facility spans 7.2 lakh sq ft and will include 110 critical-care beds, 14 modular operation theatres, a dedicated emergency tower and a 24x7 central laboratory designed to handle more than 6,000 samples a day. The new hospital is CareVista's largest single investment to date and takes the group's capacity past 7,200 beds. "Kokapet will be our flagship for transplant, neurosciences and high-end critical care, and the diagnostic backbone has to match that ambition," said Dr. Ravi Shankar Menon, Chief Medical Officer. Deepa Iyer, Head of Laboratory Services, said the group is finalising equipment for clinical chemistry, immunoassay and molecular testing and wants the lab to go live 45 days before patient admissions begin. Recruitment of about 1,400 staff, including 220 doctors, is under way.

title: CareVista Hospitals to acquire three Tamil Nadu hospitals for INR 620 crore
body: CareVista Hospitals has signed definitive agreements to acquire three hospitals in Tamil Nadu – in Madurai, Tiruchirappalli and Salem – with a combined 610 beds, for an enterprise value of INR 620 crore. The acquisition, funded through internal accruals and a debt line arranged with support from existing investor BluePeak Healthcare Partners, is expected to close by December. CareVista said it will integrate the hospitals onto its clinical protocols, procurement contracts and IT stack within 12 months of closing. "Standardising our labs, pharmacy and clinical systems is how we deliver the same outcomes in Salem as in Hyderabad," said Anil Kothari, VP Procurement, adding that equipment contracts at the three sites would be reviewed as part of integration. The deal marks CareVista's entry into Tamil Nadu and lifts its bed count to about 7,400 including projects under construction.

title: Aarogya Lifeline Hospitals raises INR 1,200 crore from BluePeak Healthcare Partners
body: Aarogya Lifeline Hospitals has raised INR 1,200 crore in a growth funding round led by private equity firm BluePeak Healthcare Partners, which will take a significant minority stake in the Lucknow-based group. The investment will fund four new hospitals in Varanasi, Gorakhpur, Dehradun and Noida, adding about 1,300 beds by 2028, as well as upgrades to its existing 11 facilities. "Tier-2 India needs tertiary care close to home, and Aarogya has shown it can build and run it profitably," said Rahul Khanna, Managing Partner at BluePeak. CEO Sanjay Prakash Tripathi said part of the capital is earmarked for a hub-and-spoke laboratory network and a single laboratory information platform across all hospitals. Neha Bansal, Director – Laboratory Medicine, will lead the diagnostics standardisation programme, the company said.

title: Aarogya Lifeline inaugurates 300-bed hospital in Varanasi, first of four new projects
body: Aarogya Lifeline Hospitals inaugurated a 300-bed multi-specialty hospital in Varanasi on Saturday, the first of four new hospital projects funded by its recent capital raise. Built at a cost of INR 380 crore, the facility has 80 ICU beds, a cath lab, eight operation theatres and a round-the-clock laboratory with automated chemistry and immunoassay lines. Outpatient services started this week and inpatient admissions will scale up over the next quarter. "Patients from eastern Uttar Pradesh and western Bihar have been travelling to Delhi or Lucknow for complex care. That changes today," said CEO Sanjay Prakash Tripathi. The group said the Gorakhpur hospital will be commissioned in mid-2027, followed by Dehradun and Noida. Imran Qureshi, Head of Procurement, said equipment tenders for Gorakhpur would be issued in the coming months.

title: Sunrise Multispeciality adds 200-bed new wing at Pune's Baner hospital
body: Sunrise Multispeciality Hospitals has begun construction of a 200-bed new wing at its Baner hospital in Pune, taking the campus to 520 beds. The INR 175 crore project, scheduled to be commissioned by March 2027, will house a mother-and-child block, a 40-bed neuro ICU and an expanded emergency department. The hospital will also relocate and double the size of its clinical laboratory to support round-the-clock testing for the enlarged campus. "Occupancy at Baner has stayed above 85 per cent for two years; the new wing lets us stop turning patients away," said Madhavi Kulkarni, Chief Operating Officer. Rohan Deshpande, Director – Biomedical Engineering, said the group is evaluating vendors for analyzers, point-of-care blood gas and a new laboratory information system to be installed before the wing opens.

title: Sunrise Multispeciality begins NABH and NABL accreditation drive across four hospitals
body: Sunrise Multispeciality Hospitals has launched a group-wide programme to secure NABH accreditation for all four of its hospitals and NABL accreditation for their laboratories within 18 months. The group has appointed an external consultant to run gap assessments and mock audits, and will upgrade quality-control processes, calibration records and sample tracking in its labs. "Accreditation is increasingly a requirement from insurers and corporate clients, and it forces discipline into how our laboratory reports every result," said Madhavi Kulkarni, Chief Operating Officer. Rohan Deshpande, Director – Biomedical Engineering, said older analyzers that cannot produce audit-ready QC logs will be replaced as part of the drive. The first laboratory audit is scheduled at the Baner hospital in February.

title: MediNova Diagnostic Labs raises USD 45 million to expand home sample collection to 40 cities
body: MediNova Diagnostic Labs has raised USD 45 million in a Series C funding round led by a global healthcare fund, with participation from BluePeak Healthcare Partners. The Bengaluru-based lab chain will use the capital to expand home sample collection to 40 cities, add 12 processing labs and build a molecular diagnostics hub in Hyderabad. MediNova currently processes about 55,000 samples a day across 38 labs. "Home collection now accounts for 42 per cent of our revenue and is growing twice as fast as walk-ins," said CEO Karthik Subramanian. The company plans to hire 1,500 phlebotomists over 18 months. Dr. Lakshmi Narayanan, Head of Laboratory Operations, said the new labs will be highly automated to keep turnaround times under six hours for routine panels.

title: MediNova Diagnostic Labs appoints Dr. Lakshmi Narayanan as Head of Laboratory Operations
body: MediNova Diagnostic Labs has appointed Dr. Lakshmi Narayanan as Head of Laboratory Operations, overseeing its network of 38 processing labs across South India. A pathologist with 22 years of experience, she joins from a large national reference laboratory where she led quality and automation. She will report to CEO Karthik Subramanian. "Lakshmi has run some of the most automated labs in the country. Her mandate is to standardise equipment, quality control and reporting across MediNova so that a patient in Madurai gets the same quality as one in Bengaluru," Subramanian said. Dr. Narayanan said her first priorities are consolidating analyzer platforms, tightening turnaround time and reviewing the company's laboratory software. The appointment follows MediNova's recent capital raise.

title: PathCrest Diagnostics acquires Jaipur-based lab chain in INR 210 crore deal
body: PathCrest Diagnostics has agreed to acquire a Jaipur-based lab chain with 11 laboratories and 160 collection centres across Rajasthan for INR 210 crore, in a move to double its presence in the state. The acquisition will be completed in two tranches, with PathCrest buying an 80 per cent stake upfront and the remainder over three years. "Rajasthan is one of the fastest-growing diagnostics markets in India and this gives us immediate scale," said Managing Director Hardik Mehta. PathCrest said it will migrate the acquired labs onto its equipment and reagent contracts and its central quality systems. Dr. Farzana Shaikh, Chief of Pathology, will lead the integration, which is expected to include replacing ageing analyzers at five of the acquired sites.

title: PathCrest targets NABL accreditation for all 24 laboratories by 2027
body: PathCrest Diagnostics has set a target of NABL accreditation for all 24 of its laboratories by December 2027, up from nine currently accredited sites. The company said it will invest in internal quality-control software, external quality assurance programmes and staff training, and will run quarterly internal audits at every laboratory. "Hospitals and corporate customers increasingly ask for accreditation before they sign contracts," said Dr. Farzana Shaikh, Chief of Pathology. "It is also the single best way to raise our own standards." She added that analyzers at smaller labs will be upgraded so that every site can produce traceable calibration and QC data. PathCrest's labs in Surat, Vadodara and Udaipur are first in line for assessment.

title: TrueLine Pathology launches home sample collection in 12 cities across eastern India
body: TrueLine Pathology Network has launched home sample collection services in 12 cities across West Bengal, Odisha, Jharkhand and Assam, backed by a fleet of 350 trained phlebotomists. Patients can book a doorstep visit through the company's app or WhatsApp, with collection slots from 6 am. Samples are transported in temperature-controlled boxes to TrueLine's central reference lab in Kolkata and four regional hubs. "People in Siliguri or Guwahati should not have to queue at a centre for a thyroid test," said founder and CEO Subhajit Banerjee. The company also plans to add 60 collection centres over the next year. Dr. Moumita Ghosh, Head of Laboratory, said the higher volumes will require additional immunoassay capacity at the regional hubs.

title: TrueLine Pathology plans lab automation and new laboratory information system rollout
body: TrueLine Pathology Network is planning a lab automation upgrade at its Kolkata reference laboratory and a switch to a cloud-based laboratory information system across all sites by mid-2027. The company said its current on-premise software cannot keep pace with rising volumes from home collection and hospital outsourcing contracts. "We want barcode-to-report digitisation, instrument middleware and auto-verification so our pathologists focus on the difficult cases," said Arindam Sen, Head of IT. Dr. Moumita Ghosh, Head of Laboratory, said the goal is to cut turnaround time for routine chemistry and hormone panels by at least 30 per cent. TrueLine has invited proposals from analyzer and software vendors and expects to shortlist partners by November.

title: OnkoCare to open 180-bed comprehensive cancer centre in Kochi
body: OnkoCare Cancer Centres will open a 180-bed comprehensive cancer centre in Kochi in March 2027, its tenth facility and first in Kerala. The INR 420 crore centre will offer surgical, medical and radiation oncology, with two linear accelerators, a bone marrow transplant unit and a dedicated molecular oncology laboratory. "Kerala has one of the highest cancer incidence rates in India, yet many patients still travel to Chennai or Bengaluru for advanced treatment," said Dr. Thomas Varghese, Chief Medical Officer. Dr. Shalini Rao, Head – Laboratory & Molecular Oncology, said the lab will run tumour markers, flow cytometry and PCR-based mutation testing on site, reducing reliance on external reference labs. Hiring for the oncology team starts next month.

title: OnkoCare appoints Dr. Thomas Varghese as Chief Medical Officer
body: OnkoCare Cancer Centres has appointed Dr. Thomas Varghese as Chief Medical Officer, effective immediately. Dr. Varghese, a medical oncologist with 25 years of experience, previously led the oncology division of a large South Indian hospital group. He will oversee clinical quality, protocols and expansion across OnkoCare's nine cancer centres, including the new Kochi project. "Our growth plan needs a clinical leader who can standardise care pathways, diagnostics and outcomes reporting across every centre," said the company's chairman. Dr. Varghese said he intends to review laboratory and molecular testing arrangements, which are currently split between in-house labs and external partners, within his first six months.

title: Hridaya Heart Institute to build cardiac centre of excellence with three cath labs in Jaipur
body: Hridaya Heart Institute will build a 220-bed cardiac centre of excellence in Jaipur with three cath labs, a hybrid operating theatre and a heart transplant programme, at an investment of INR 260 crore. The facility, scheduled to open in late 2027, will be the group's sixth heart institute. "Rajasthan performs fewer than half the angioplasties it needs; we want to close that gap," said Dr. Vikram Singh Rathore, Medical Director. Manish Agarwal, VP Operations, said the centre will include a 24x7 stat laboratory for cardiac markers such as high-sensitivity troponin and NT-proBNP, as well as point-of-care coagulation testing in the cath labs and ICU. Equipment procurement is expected to begin in the first quarter of next year.

title: Hridaya Heart Institute seeks JCI accreditation for flagship Udaipur hospital
body: Hridaya Heart Institute has started preparations for JCI accreditation of its flagship Udaipur hospital, aiming to attract international and insurance-backed patients. The group said a mock survey will be held in December, followed by the formal accreditation audit next year. Its laboratories are also being prepared for NABL renewal. "International accreditation tells patients abroad that our processes meet a global benchmark," said Kavita Sharma, Quality & Accreditation Manager. She said the laboratory's quality-control documentation, turnaround-time monitoring and critical-value reporting are being overhauled, and some analyzers will be replaced to meet traceability requirements. Hridaya treats about 1,200 international patients a year, mainly from East Africa and the Gulf.

title: Dhanvantari Institute of Medical Sciences to add 750-bed new hospital block in Mysuru
body: Dhanvantari Institute of Medical Sciences will build a 750-bed new hospital block on its Mysuru campus, raising total teaching-hospital capacity to 1,650 beds as it prepares to increase MBBS intake to 250 seats and add postgraduate courses. The INR 540 crore project includes a super-speciality block, a 60-bed emergency department and a new central laboratory integrating biochemistry, microbiology and pathology. "The regulator's norms tie seats to beds and lab infrastructure, and we want to be well ahead of those requirements," said Dean Dr. Prakash Gowda. Dr. Anitha Ramesh, Head of Biochemistry and Central Lab, said the college will move to fully automated analyzers and a laboratory information system integrated with the hospital's records. The first phase is due to be commissioned in 2027.

title: Dhanvantari medical college central laboratory applies for NABL accreditation
body: The central laboratory at Dhanvantari Institute of Medical Sciences has applied for NABL accreditation, the institute said, as part of a broader quality push ahead of its hospital expansion. The laboratory processes about 3,500 samples a day across biochemistry, haematology, microbiology and serology. "Accreditation improves patient safety and also teaches our residents how a modern laboratory is run," said Dr. Anitha Ramesh, Professor and Head of Biochemistry. The institute has engaged assessors for a pre-audit and is upgrading internal quality control, external quality assurance participation and equipment calibration records. Dr. Ramesh said two older chemistry analyzers will be retired before the final assessment.

title: Deccan State Health Services Corporation floats tender for diagnostic services in 42 district hospitals
body: Deccan State Health Services Corporation has floated an e-tender for hub-and-spoke diagnostic services covering 42 district hospitals and 310 community health centres, with an estimated contract value of INR 320 crore over five years. Selected bidders must install and operate clinical chemistry, immunoassay and haematology analyzers, supply reagents and deploy a laboratory information system that links every district hospital with the state health mission's dashboard. The procurement requires results within four hours for inpatient samples and 24 hours for spokes. "The aim is to make 120 tests free at every district hospital," said Managing Director Suresh Babu Reddy. The pre-bid meeting is scheduled for October 8 and bids close on November 5.

title: State corporation seeks point-of-care analyzers for 1,800 primary health centres
body: Deccan State Health Services Corporation has issued a tender for the procurement of point-of-care analyzers and rapid test kits for 1,800 primary health centres, valued at about INR 88 crore. The government corporation is seeking semi-automated chemistry analyzers, HbA1c and haemoglobin meters and rapid kits for malaria, dengue, typhoid and hepatitis, along with training and five-year maintenance. "Primary health centres must be able to diagnose common conditions on the spot instead of referring patients to the district," said Dr. Padmaja Rao, General Manager – Equipment & Diagnostics. Bidders must demonstrate installations in at least two Indian states. Technical bids are due within 30 days.

title: Vindhya Medical Supplies Corporation issues RFP for RT-PCR kits and molecular lab upgrades
body: Vindhya Medical Supplies Corporation has issued an RFP for RT-PCR kits, nucleic acid extraction systems and molecular lab upgrades across 18 government medical colleges and district hospitals, with an estimated value of INR 145 crore. The procurement covers tuberculosis, hepatitis B and C, HPV and respiratory virus panels under the state health mission. "We want every medical college to run its own molecular diagnostics rather than depending on two referral labs," said Rajendra Chouhan, Chief General Manager – Procurement. Dr. Meera Dubey, Deputy Director – Laboratory Services, said bidders must also provide software for sample tracking and reporting. The pre-bid meeting is set for October 14.

title: HomeLab Express raises USD 18 million to take home sample collection to 25 cities
body: HomeLab Express, a Bengaluru-based home sample collection startup, has raised USD 18 million in Series B funding to expand from eight to 25 cities and set up its own processing labs. The company currently completes about 9,000 home collection visits a day through 1,100 phlebotomists and partner labs. "Partner labs got us here, but to control turnaround and quality we need our own labs in the top cities," said co-founder and CEO Aditya Rao. The first two company-owned labs, in Bengaluru and Pune, will be commissioned by early 2027. Sneha Pillai, Head of Lab Partnerships, said HomeLab is evaluating analyzer vendors and a cloud laboratory system that can connect directly to its booking app.

title: CliniQ Connect adds at-home testing and doorstep phlebotomists to its telehealth app
body: Telehealth platform CliniQ Connect has launched at-home testing in 15 cities, allowing users to book home sample collection immediately after a video consultation. The company has hired 400 phlebotomists and will route samples to a mix of partner labs and two collection centres it operates in Delhi NCR. "About a third of our consultations end with a lab prescription, and half of those patients never got tested. At-home testing fixes that leak," said Nikhil Jain, Chief Operating Officer. Dr. Ayesha Khan, Medical Director, said reports will flow directly into the patient's record on the app and to the consulting doctor. CliniQ also plans to offer point-of-care tests such as HbA1c and lipid profiles at doorstep visits.

title: Nilgiri Health Group to open 350-bed new hospital in Coimbatore's Saravanampatti
body: Nilgiri Health Group will open a 350-bed new hospital in Saravanampatti, Coimbatore, in February 2027, investing INR 310 crore in the project. The multi-specialty hospital will include 90 critical-care beds, a transplant unit and a central laboratory that will also serve as a reference lab for the group's other five hospitals. "This is our largest project and will anchor our hub-and-spoke model in western Tamil Nadu," said Managing Director Senthil Kumar Palanisamy. Dr. Revathi Krishnan, Head of Laboratory Medicine, said the reference lab will be designed for automation and will be accredited from day one. Gokul Ramaswamy, General Manager – Purchase, said equipment orders will be placed by December.

title: Nilgiri Health Group appoints Dr. Revathi Krishnan as Head of Laboratory Medicine
body: Nilgiri Health Group has appointed Dr. Revathi Krishnan as Head of Laboratory Medicine, a new group-level role created to consolidate laboratory operations across its six hospitals. Dr. Krishnan was previously head of laboratory at a large Bengaluru teaching hospital and has led two NABL accreditation projects. She will report to Managing Director Senthil Kumar Palanisamy. "We are moving from six independent hospital labs to one network with a reference lab at the centre," Palanisamy said. "Revathi's job is to design that network." Dr. Krishnan said she will review analyzer contracts, reagent spend and the group's laboratory software in her first quarter.

title: GulfCare Medical Group to launch oncology centre of excellence in Abu Dhabi
body: GulfCare Medical Group will open a USD 95 million oncology centre of excellence in Abu Dhabi in the second half of 2027, adding 120 beds, radiation therapy bunkers and a day-care chemotherapy unit. The centre will also house a cancer genomics and molecular laboratory. "More than a third of cancer patients from the UAE still seek treatment abroad; we want to bring that care home," said Dr. Faisal Al Mansoori, Group Chief Medical Officer. Priya Menon, Director – Laboratory Services, said the lab will run tumour markers, immunohistochemistry and PCR-based testing, and will be connected to the group's laboratory information system across four hospitals and 30 clinics.

title: Lionpoint Healthcare acquires Malaysian lab operator for USD 38 million
body: Singapore-based Lionpoint Healthcare has agreed to acquire a Kuala Lumpur laboratory operator with 16 labs and 90 collection points for USD 38 million, its largest acquisition to date. The deal gives Lionpoint a reference lab in Malaysia and more than doubles its daily test volumes. "The acquisition lets us serve our clinics in Malaysia with our own diagnostics and gives us scale to negotiate better on equipment and reagents," said Group CEO Daniel Tan Wei Ming. Dr. Grace Lim, Head of Laboratory, said the integration plan includes moving both networks onto a common laboratory information system and harmonising analyzer platforms over two years. Completion is expected in the first quarter of 2027.

title: Savannah Diagnostics raises USD 12 million to expand across East Africa
body: Nairobi-based Savannah Diagnostics has raised USD 12 million in funding from a consortium of impact investors to open 30 new branches and a molecular reference laboratory. The investment will take the chain into Rwanda and expand its presence in Uganda and Tanzania. "Accurate diagnosis is still the weakest link in East African healthcare," said CEO Wanjiru Kamau. Laboratory Director Dr. Otieno Ochieng said the new reference laboratory in Nairobi will run HIV viral load, TB and hepatitis PCR, and the company will pursue international accreditation for it. Savannah plans to standardise analyzers across its network and roll out a cloud laboratory system that allows doctors to view results on mobile phones.

title: Padma General Hospital adds 250-bed new wing in Dhaka
body: Padma General Hospital will add a 250-bed new wing to its Dhaka campus, taking capacity to 770 beds, at a cost of about USD 42 million. The wing, scheduled to be commissioned in 2027, will house a cardiac unit, a 50-bed ICU and an expanded laboratory and blood bank. "Demand for quality private care in Dhaka keeps rising and our occupancy has been above 90 per cent for over a year," said CEO Dr. Rezaul Karim. Nusrat Jahan, Head of Procurement, said the hospital is inviting proposals for laboratory analyzers, point-of-care testing and hospital information systems, and would prefer vendors that can offer local service support. The expansion also includes 12 diagnostic collection centres in the city.

title: Matrika Women & Child to open three new hospitals with 360 beds by 2027
body: Matrika Women & Child Hospitals plans to open three new hospitals in Hyderabad, Nashik and Hubballi with a combined 360 beds by the end of 2027, investing INR 160 crore. Each hospital will have a neonatal ICU, labour and delivery suites and an in-house laboratory for maternal and neonatal testing. "The first new hospital in Hyderabad's Kompally will be commissioned in April," said Vivek Patil, VP Projects. Dr. Sunita Joshi, Chief Medical Officer, said the group wants rapid bedside testing for neonatal bilirubin, blood gases and sepsis markers in every NICU, and a standard lab setup across its 17 facilities once the new hospitals open.

title: Kaveri Kidney Care to set up transplant centre of excellence in Bengaluru
body: Kaveri Kidney Care will set up a 120-bed kidney and liver transplant centre of excellence in Bengaluru at an investment of INR 95 crore. The centre will include dedicated transplant ICUs, an HLA and immunology laboratory and a therapeutic drug monitoring service for immunosuppressants. "We perform about 180 kidney transplants a year today and want to reach 400 within three years," said Dr. Harish Nagaraj, Managing Director. Bhavana Shetty, Operations Manager – Labs, said the new lab will also support the group's 60 dialysis centres with routine renal panels, and the company is evaluating analyzer and reagent partners. The transplant centre is expected to open by September 2027.

title: Samarth Hospitals appoints Dr. Manasi Bhonsle as Chief Medical Officer
body: Samarth Hospitals has appointed Dr. Manasi Bhonsle as Chief Medical Officer, responsible for clinical quality across its seven hospitals. Dr. Bhonsle, a critical-care specialist, was earlier medical director at a large Mumbai hospital. "Samarth is entering a new phase of growth, and we need consistent protocols, diagnostics and quality metrics across every hospital," said Chairman and Managing Director Ashok Wankhede. Dr. Bhonsle said she will prioritise infection control, laboratory turnaround time for emergency and ICU patients, and preparing all hospitals for NABH assessment. She will work closely with Sachin Tidke, Manager – Biomedical & Procurement, on equipment standardisation.

title: Samarth Hospitals raises INR 450 crore private equity investment for Raipur and Warangal expansion
body: Samarth Hospitals has raised INR 450 crore in private equity investment from BluePeak Healthcare Partners, which will acquire a 26 per cent stake in the Nagpur-based chain. The funding will be used to build hospitals in Raipur and Warangal and to acquire a 150-bed hospital in Amravati. "Central India remains under-served for tertiary care and Samarth has the clinical depth to fill that gap," said Rahul Khanna of BluePeak. Chairman Ashok Wankhede said the group will centralise laboratory and procurement functions as part of the expansion. The transaction is subject to regulatory approvals and is expected to close within 90 days.

title: Ekam Genomics molecular laboratory secures NABL accreditation, plans RT-PCR capacity expansion
body: Chennai-based Ekam Genomics has received NABL accreditation for its molecular laboratory, covering RT-PCR panels for respiratory viruses, tuberculosis and sexually transmitted infections, as well as its oncology testing. The company said the accreditation will help it win hospital outsourcing contracts and government programmes. "Accreditation was an 11-month journey that touched every process, from sample receipt to report sign-off," said Meenakshi Sundar, Head of Quality. Co-founder Dr. Arvind Raghavan said Ekam will triple RT-PCR capacity to 4,000 samples a day and add automated extraction systems by early next year. The laboratory now plans to seek CAP-style international audit readiness for its genomics unit.

title: JeevanRekha Charitable Hospital to build 150-bed oncology block with radiation therapy
body: JeevanRekha Charitable Hospital in Indore will build a 150-bed oncology block with two radiation therapy bunkers, a day-care chemotherapy ward and a cancer centre laboratory, at a cost of INR 120 crore raised largely from donors and a state grant. "More than 40 per cent of our cancer patients come from rural Madhya Pradesh and cannot afford to travel to Mumbai," said Dr. Alok Verma, Medical Superintendent. The hospital expects to commission the block in 18 months. Ritu Saxena, Head – Purchase & Stores, said procurement for linear accelerators, laboratory analyzers for tumour markers and a new hospital information system will begin early next year.

title: Arogyam Neighbourhood Clinics adds two outlets in Chennai suburbs
body: Arogyam Neighbourhood Clinics has added two outlets in Tambaram and Porur, taking its chain of primary care clinics in Chennai to 20. Each clinic has two general practitioners, a small pharmacy counter and a nurse who can draw blood for basic tests, which are sent to a partner lab. "Families want a doctor they know, five minutes from home, and they want to be seen without a long wait," said founder Dr. Kavya Sundaram. The company, which is funded by its founders and a small group of angel investors, said it may consider more locations next year depending on footfall. Consultation fees start at INR 250.

title: CareVista said to be scouting land in Kolkata for possible eastern foray
body: CareVista Hospitals is said to be scouting land parcels in Kolkata's New Town and Rajarhat areas as it weighs an entry into eastern India, according to two people familiar with the matter. No decision has been taken, and the discussions are at a preliminary stage, the people said. A CareVista spokesperson declined to comment on what the company described as market speculation. The Hyderabad-based group has so far focused on South and West India. Industry observers note that several hospital operators have looked at Kolkata over the past decade, citing strong demand for tertiary care, but land costs and approvals have slowed plans. Any project would likely take four to five years to complete.

title: Lionpoint Healthcare exploring options in Indonesia, says group CEO
body: Lionpoint Healthcare is studying the Indonesian primary care market, Group CEO Daniel Tan Wei Ming told reporters on the sidelines of a Singapore industry conference, but said the company had no concrete plans yet. "Indonesia is a huge opportunity and we would be foolish not to look at it, but we are still learning the regulatory landscape," he said. Tan said the group's immediate priority remained its existing clinics in Singapore and Malaysia, where patient visits rose 9 per cent last year. He did not rule out partnerships with local operators as a possible route. Analysts said any entry would likely be at least two years away.

title: GulfCare Medical Group eyes Saudi Arabia as regional demand grows
body: GulfCare Medical Group is evaluating opportunities in Saudi Arabia as private healthcare demand in the kingdom grows, a senior executive said at a Dubai healthcare forum. Group Chief Medical Officer Dr. Faisal Al Mansoori said the company was "watching the market closely" and had held early conversations with potential local partners, but declined to give a timeline. "Our focus for the next 18 months is to deliver the projects we have already announced in the UAE," he said. The group operates four hospitals and 30 clinics in Abu Dhabi, Dubai and Sharjah. Market consultants expect significant private-sector participation in the Saudi health system over the coming decade.

title: Padma General Hospital in talks with overseas hospitals for clinical partnership
body: Padma General Hospital is in talks with hospitals in Thailand and India for a clinical partnership that could include doctor exchanges, second opinions and joint training, CEO Dr. Rezaul Karim said. The discussions are at an early stage and no agreement has been signed. "Many Bangladeshi patients travel abroad for treatment. If we can bring that expertise here through partnerships, we keep patients closer to their families," Karim said. The hospital said it would announce details once talks conclude. Padma General currently treats about 1,500 outpatients a day at its Dhaka campus and runs several diagnostic centres across the city.

title: Kaveri Kidney Care considering more dialysis units in tier-3 towns
body: Kaveri Kidney Care is considering adding dialysis units in tier-3 towns in Karnataka, Managing Director Dr. Harish Nagaraj said, as the prevalence of chronic kidney disease rises across the region. "Patients in smaller towns travel three or four hours, three times a week, for dialysis. That is not sustainable," he said. Nagaraj said the company was studying potential locations and partnership models, including public-private arrangements with district authorities, but had not finalised any plan. Kaveri currently runs 60 dialysis units across Karnataka and Tamil Nadu. The company said any expansion would be phased over several years.

title: Matrika Women & Child weighing entry into fertility care
body: Matrika Women & Child Hospitals is weighing an entry into fertility care, Chief Medical Officer Dr. Sunita Joshi said, pointing to strong demand from couples in its existing catchment areas. "Many of our obstetric patients ask us about IVF, and at the moment we refer them elsewhere," she said. Joshi said the group was assessing whether to build in-house fertility units or partner with an established IVF provider, and that a decision was unlikely before the next financial year. Matrika operates 14 facilities across Maharashtra, Karnataka and Telangana and delivered more than 21,000 babies last year.

title: Arogyam pilots evening doorstep visits by nurses for elderly patients
body: Arogyam Neighbourhood Clinics has started a small pilot in which nurses make evening doorstep visits to elderly patients registered at three of its Chennai clinics, checking blood pressure and blood sugar and reviewing medicines. About 120 patients are enrolled in the pilot. "Many of our older patients find it hard to come to the clinic after dark," said founder Dr. Kavya Sundaram. She said the company would review results after six months before deciding whether to extend the service. Arogyam has not disclosed pricing for the visits, which are currently offered free to members of its annual care plan.

title: Savannah Diagnostics in discussions with insurers on cashless test packages
body: Savannah Diagnostics is in discussions with three Kenyan health insurers to offer cashless preventive test packages for their members, CEO Wanjiru Kamau said. Under the proposal, insured patients would be able to walk into any Savannah branch for an annual health check without paying upfront. "Insurers want members to catch problems early, and we want to make testing easy," Kamau said. No agreement has been signed, and terms including pricing are still under negotiation. Savannah operates 45 branches across Kenya, Uganda and Tanzania, serving about 3,000 patients a day.

title: MediNova CEO hints at North India entry 'at the right time'
body: MediNova Diagnostic Labs could eventually enter North India, CEO Karthik Subramanian said at an industry event, but added that the company's near-term focus remains the four southern states where it operates. "North India is a large market and we will go there at the right time, possibly through a partner," Subramanian said. He declined to give a timeline or name any cities. MediNova has built its business around hospital outsourcing contracts and corporate wellness programmes in South India. Analysts say competition in Delhi NCR and Punjab is intense, with several national chains already present.

title: CareVista wins patient experience award at national healthcare summit
body: CareVista Hospitals won the patient experience award in the large hospital group category at a national healthcare summit held in New Delhi on Friday. The jury cited the group's nurse-led discharge programme, which cut average discharge time from five hours to under two, and its multilingual patient helpline. "This recognition belongs to our nurses and front-office teams, who make the difference patients remember," said Dr. Ravi Shankar Menon. The summit, now in its ninth edition, recognised 34 hospitals and clinics across 12 categories. CareVista also received a special mention for its patient feedback programme, which collects more than 40,000 responses a month.

title: Consumer commission orders PathCrest to pay INR 2.5 lakh over delayed report
body: A district consumer disputes redressal commission in Ahmedabad has directed PathCrest Diagnostics to pay INR 2.5 lakh in compensation to a patient who alleged that a delayed report led to a missed surgery date in 2024. The commission held that the company had failed to communicate the delay in time, though it rejected the complainant's claim of an incorrect result. PathCrest said it respected the order and was reviewing its legal options. "Patient communication is a priority and we have since strengthened our alert processes," a spokesperson said. The complainant had sought INR 20 lakh in damages.

title: Nilgiri Health Group holds free eye screening camp for 2,000 farm workers
body: Nilgiri Health Group conducted a free eye screening camp in Pollachi over the weekend, examining more than 2,000 farm workers and their families as part of its community outreach programme. Ophthalmologists and optometrists from the group's hospitals screened participants for cataract, refractive errors and diabetic eye disease, and distributed 700 pairs of spectacles free of charge. "Many of these workers had never had an eye test," said Managing Director Senthil Kumar Palanisamy. Patients needing cataract surgery will be operated on free of cost over the next two months. The group has held 45 such camps across western Tamil Nadu this year.

title: Aarogya Lifeline reports 18% revenue growth in first quarter
body: Aarogya Lifeline Hospitals reported an 18 per cent rise in revenue to INR 740 crore for the quarter ended June, driven by higher occupancy and a larger share of insured patients. Operating profit margin improved by 120 basis points to 21.4 per cent, while net profit rose 24 per cent to INR 96 crore. Average revenue per occupied bed-day increased 7 per cent. "Our mature hospitals continue to deliver steady margins, and payer mix is moving in the right direction," said CEO Sanjay Prakash Tripathi. The company kept its full-year guidance unchanged. Shares rose 2.1 per cent in afternoon trade after the results.

title: Hridaya Heart Institute walkathon draws 8,000 participants on World Heart Day
body: More than 8,000 people took part in a 5 km walkathon organised by Hridaya Heart Institute in Jaipur on World Heart Day, the largest edition of the annual event so far. Participants included schoolchildren, senior citizens and members of local running clubs. Doctors from the institute spoke about the importance of regular exercise, quitting tobacco and controlling blood pressure. "Prevention is still the most powerful medicine we have," said Dr. Vikram Singh Rathore. Free blood pressure checks were offered at the finish line. The institute said it would hold similar walks in Udaipur and Indore next year.

title: Vitalis Life Sciences posts 11% profit growth on strong vaccine exports
body: Vitalis Life Sciences reported an 11 per cent increase in net profit to INR 312 crore for the June quarter, as exports of paediatric vaccines to Africa and Latin America offset weaker domestic sales. Revenue rose 9 per cent to INR 2,150 crore. The company said pricing pressure in the domestic generic injectables segment persisted. "Our export order book gives us good visibility for the rest of the year," said CEO Dr. Kiran Chandra. Research and development spending stood at 8.2 per cent of revenue. The board declared an interim dividend of INR 4 per share.

title: Samarth College of Nursing holds convocation for 180 graduates
body: The Samarth College of Nursing, run by the Samarth Hospitals group, held its annual convocation in Nagpur on Sunday, awarding degrees and diplomas to 180 nursing graduates. Chairman and Managing Director Ashok Wankhede congratulated the graduates and said nurses remain the backbone of patient care. Gold medals were presented to the top three students in the BSc Nursing programme. "Several of our graduates will join hospitals across Maharashtra, and many will serve in rural areas," said the college principal. The college, founded in 2012, has trained more than 1,800 nurses to date.

title: MediNova Diagnostic Labs launches brand campaign with film actor
body: MediNova Diagnostic Labs has launched a multi-city brand campaign featuring a popular Kannada film actor, focusing on preventive health checks for adults above 35. The campaign spans television, outdoor hoardings, social media and cinema advertising across Karnataka, Tamil Nadu, Kerala and Telangana. "We want preventive testing to feel as routine as an annual car service," said CEO Karthik Subramanian. The campaign, created by a Bengaluru-based creative agency, will run through the festive season. MediNova said it would also run a customer referral programme during the campaign period.

title: GulfCare Medical Group named official medical partner for Abu Dhabi marathon
body: GulfCare Medical Group has been named the official medical partner for this year's Abu Dhabi marathon, which is expected to draw more than 20,000 runners in December. The group will deploy doctors, nurses and paramedics at 15 medical stations along the route and at the finish area. "Keeping runners safe while encouraging an active lifestyle fits naturally with what we do," said Dr. Faisal Al Mansoori. GulfCare will also run free pre-race health talks for registered participants. The group has supported community sports events in the UAE for the past six years.

title: Dhanvantari students win inter-college medical quiz for third straight year
body: A team of final-year MBBS students from Dhanvantari Institute of Medical Sciences won the south zone inter-college medical quiz in Mangaluru for the third year in a row, beating 46 teams. The three-member team answered questions on anatomy, pharmacology, community medicine and clinical case scenarios. "Our students combine strong fundamentals with hands-on clinical exposure," said Dean Dr. Prakash Gowda. The winning team will represent the south zone at the national finals in Chandigarh in January. The institute also won the best poster award at the accompanying student research conference.

title: CareVista's new 500-bed Bengaluru hospital campus to run on rooftop solar and battery storage
body: CareVista Hospitals will build a 500-bed new hospital campus in Bengaluru's Whitefield that will draw a large share of its power from a 2.4 MW rooftop and car-park solar installation backed by a 5 MWh battery energy storage system. The INR 1,100 crore greenfield project, spread over 9 acres, is designed for green building certification and will include a 120-bed critical-care tower, a transplant unit and a central laboratory. "Hospitals run 24x7 and power quality is life-critical. Solar plus storage cuts our energy bill and gives us resilience during grid outages," said Anil Kothari, VP Procurement. The company is inviting proposals from solar EPC and storage vendors, while medical equipment and lab procurement will start in 2027. The campus is scheduled to open in 2028.

title: Vitalis Life Sciences to build INR 180 crore vaccine cold-chain distribution hub
body: Vitalis Life Sciences will build a vaccine and biologics cold-chain distribution hub near Hyderabad's airport at an investment of INR 180 crore. The 2.2 lakh sq ft facility will include 2-8°C and -25°C storage zones, a -70°C ultra-cold room for mRNA products and automated pallet handling, and will serve as the company's national distribution centre as well as an export gateway. "Temperature excursions are the single biggest risk to vaccine quality. This hub gives us end-to-end visibility from our plant to the airport," said Swati Mishra, Head – Supply Chain. Vitalis is evaluating third-party logistics partners, reefer fleet operators and temperature-monitoring vendors. Operations are expected to begin in late 2027.

title: Vitalis Life Sciences to set up medical-device electronics plant in Gujarat
body: Vitalis Life Sciences will invest INR 260 crore in a medical-device electronics plant in Sanand, Gujarat, to manufacture glucose meters, pulse oximeters, infusion pumps and point-of-care test readers. The facility will include SMT lines for printed circuit board assembly, a cleanroom for biosensor and microfluidic cartridge production, and in-house reliability testing. "We import most of the chips, sensors and displays today. Localising board assembly and working with Indian semiconductor partners reduces lead times and cost," said CEO Dr. Kiran Chandra. The company is seeking suppliers for microcontrollers, analog front-end chips and display modules. Commercial production is planned for mid-2027, with an initial capacity of 3 million devices a year.

title: Aarogya Lifeline to switch 150 ambulances and staff shuttles to electric vehicles
body: Aarogya Lifeline Hospitals will replace 150 ambulances, staff shuttles and sample-transport vans with electric vehicles over the next two years, at a cost of about INR 42 crore. The group is also installing 60 fast chargers across its 11 hospitals and planned new sites. "Our fleet runs around the clock between hospitals, collection points and patients' homes. Electric vehicles cut our running costs by more than half and reduce pollution around our campuses," said CEO Sanjay Prakash Tripathi. The company said it is inviting proposals from EV makers, ambulance body builders and charging operators. The first 40 vehicles, including refrigerated vans for moving blood and laboratory samples, will be deployed by March.

title: GulfCare Medical Group builds private cloud and edge data centre to digitise four hospitals
body: GulfCare Medical Group will invest USD 60 million in a private cloud, a Tier III edge data centre in Dubai and a private 5G network connecting its four hospitals and 30 clinics. The programme will host a new electronic medical record, imaging archives and the group's laboratory information system, and enable real-time monitoring of ICU patients. "Healthcare data in the UAE must stay in the country, and we need low-latency links for imaging and remote monitoring," said Priya Menon, Director – Laboratory Services, who is part of the steering committee. GulfCare is seeking partners for data centre infrastructure, networking and cybersecurity. The first phase goes live in the second quarter of 2027.
